_meta.purpose: Per-block fixtures for the offline setting check (instances.py) and the site look (../site-look/site_look.py). `attributes` is the plain block, as a new node renders it, with the stand-ins it needs to render offline at all; the site look draws it alone. `checkAttributes` is what the check adds to test a part's settings (a shown label, a background image, a content width); instances.py::check_fixture lays it over `attributes` for every render the check plans (split_fixtures.py decides and guards the split). Also per block: variants, partner preconditions, children, parents and paint states, plus `harness` (the render harness options: stubWoocommerce, renderFile, postFile, productFile, attachmentsFile; paths relative to this folder) and `post` (steps the renderer applies to the rendered markup, standing in for a view script). Seeded from calibration's fixture file, retired 2026-11-23, and the motion render paths (see each block's `notes`); Fill reads these entries too (computed-route lib/setting-record.mjs::recordFixtures).

_shared.purpose: Partners and reasons for settings every block receives from a shared extension; a block's own preconditions win.

unvalued.sgsCustomCss: free CSS the client writes: it paints whatever its text says, so no placement can be recorded for it (includes/custom-css.php::render_custom_css)

notes.sgsChildWidth: includes/child-sizing.php returns before reading sgsChildWidth unless sgsChildSizing holds a mode; the width is read by fixed.

notes: iconBackground and iconBackgroundHover: includes/helpers-button-icon-circle.php::sgs_button_icon_circle_css writes `.sgs-button__icon[data-sgs-mc~="translate"]` rules, and the attribute is written onto the icon by includes/motion/class-sgs-motion-emitter.php (data-sgs-mc) through Sgs_Motion_Renderer's render_block filter, only when the block carries a motion document on its `icon` element that writes the translate channel. The preconditions above hold that document (an ambient float; renders data-sgs-mc="translate scale" on the icon with the runner's --render-block-filters). `sgsMotion` is not in block.json's attributes, so instances.py::preconditions (it keeps an attribute only when `a in schema`) must accept it before these two entries take effect.

attributes.question: What will you use them for?
attributes.intro: Your prescription tells you which. If there's an “ADD” column on it, varifocal is probably what you're after.

options.label: Distance
options.helpText: Uses the main line of your prescription. This is what most people want in sunglasses — sharp vision looking ahead and into the distance.

options.label: Reading
options.helpText: For reading in the garden or by the pool. Uses the “ADD” value on your prescription. You won't want to drive in these.

options.label: Varifocal
options.helpText: Distance at the top, reading at the bottom, blended in between with no visible line. Usually for over-40s. I take the fitting measurements from a photo or in person.
options.description: Near and far in one lens, no line.

options.label: No prescription
options.helpText: Adds the frame to your bag exactly as the brand made it, with its original tinted lenses. You can always add prescription lenses later.
options.description: Keep the lenses they come with.

attributes.question: How thin would you like them?
attributes.intro: Thinner lenses are lighter and sit neater in the frame. If you don't know your numbers, Standard is a safe pick — I'll check when your prescription arrives and tell you if something thinner is worth it.

options.label: Standard · 1.5
options.helpText: The standard lens material. Perfectly good for a mild prescription — going thinner would make no visible difference and cost you money for nothing.
options.description: Fine for most prescriptions up to about ±2.00.

options.label: Thin · 1.6
options.helpText: Noticeably slimmer at the edge and lighter on your nose. The usual choice once your prescription gets past about ±2.00.

options.label: Extra thin · 1.67
options.helpText: Worth it for a stronger prescription — it stops the lens edge standing proud of the frame and reduces the way strong lenses distort how your eyes look.

options.label: Ultra thin · 1.74
options.helpText: The thinnest lens material available. If your prescription is strong, this is the difference between glasses you want to wear and glasses you tolerate.
options.description: The thinnest made. For ±6.00 and above.

The basket state ($state) is read only on the cart or checkout page (is_cart() or is_checkout(), WC()->cart): fixtures/free-delivery-bar-wc.php stands in a cart page with a basket of 45.00 (get_subtotal, get_subtotal_tax, is_empty, needs_shipping). The card then prints the message with the amount left, the fill's --sgs-free-delivery-bar-pct and aria-valuenow, and (hideWhenEmpty on, basket not empty) no hidden attribute.

The second variant lowers the override to 30, below the basket: the card reaches the complete state (includes/helpers-free-delivery.php::sgs_free_delivery_progress, render.php::$classes), which adds sgs-free-delivery-bar--complete and the success message.
Seeded by seed_fixtures.py from calibration's fixture file (retired 2026-11-23) and render-paths.json; the entry was then corrected, as follows.

The second variant held layout as the string "carousel", but layout is a per-device object ({desktop,tablet,mobile}, block.json attributes.layout): instances.py::_object_values reads the held value's desktop tier and raised AttributeError ('str' object has no attribute 'get'). The variant now holds the object, carousel at every device, because sgs_gallery_layout_tiers honours a carousel only when all three tiers are carousel (src/blocks/gallery/render.php::$sgs_gal_tiers).

mediaItems held the retired flat shape (id, url, mime at the item's top level); render.php::$images reads each item's picture or video from source.<device> ({kind,id,url,width,height}), so the old items drew nothing. They now follow the render paths' attachment and media-slot paths: two images with an attachment id (11 and 12, in harness.attachments, so wp_get_attachment_image() draws them), an image with no id (the shared media renderer draws it) and a video (the media renderer's video markup). showCaptions is true, so each item draws its caption; enableLightbox is true by default, so each tile sits in the lightbox trigger.

src/blocks/gift-order/render.php returns before printing unless the class SGS\Blocks\Gift_Order\Gift_Order_Store_Api exists, and prints its own parts (switch, checkbox, help line, note field, count, error line) only on a single-product page (includes/gift-order/helpers-gift-order-product.php::sgs_gift_order_is_product_page reads is_product(); elsewhere it prints one empty placeholder for the Cart and Checkout blocks' component): fixtures/gift-order-wc.php loads includes/gift-order/class-gift-order-session.php and class-gift-order-store-api.php and answers is_product() true.

basketHelp holds text, so the help line prints (includes/gift-order/helpers-gift-order-product.php::sgs_gift_order_product_html, $config['basketHelp'] !== ''), and messagePlaceholder holds a placeholder for the note field.

The stand-in WooCommerce session (WC_Session::get for the key sgs_gift_order; includes/gift-order/class-gift-order-session.php::get) holds on true, a name and a note, so the fields print open (no hidden attribute on sgs-gift-order__fields) with the note and its count line. checked() and esc_textarea(), which the runner's stubs lack, are defined in the stand-in file.
